subtopic: Being idolised or hated by juniors
passage:
Kwame had a habit he only noticed on a Thursday night, when he heard himself say, "You know I'd do it myself, but you're the only one I trust with this." Rania and two other juniors stayed until nine that week. He had said almost the same words the week before.

Driving home, he replayed their faces. They had looked proud. He had liked that a little too much, and he had liked how it kept the client from seeing his own late slides.

On Friday he called the team together in the small meeting room. "I need to correct something. I asked you to stay late partly because I was behind, and partly because I enjoy being needed. That wasn't fair. From now on I'll say what I need and you can say no."

Rania looked surprised, then nodded slowly. "Thank you for saying it."

qa.q: How many juniors stayed late with Rania on the Thursday?
qa.a: Two other juniors stayed with Rania until nine.

qa.q: What did Kwame realise about himself while driving home?
qa.a: Kwame realised he enjoyed the juniors' admiration and had used it to get them to work late and cover for his own late slides.

qa.q: What could Kwame do to keep his requests honest from now on?
qa.a: He could state the real need and the deadline plainly, and check whether each junior can say no without worrying about how he will see them.

qa.q: How might Rania have felt hearing the correction?
qa.a: Rania was probably surprised and a little relieved, because being told the truth respects the juniors more than flattery does.

grounding: Kwame notices he uses juniors' admiration to get late work and protect his image, stops, and speaks honestly about his needs.

passage:
At the small NGO office in Jalpaiguri, the new field workers called Bidisha "didi" and hung on her words. One Friday at six she found herself saying, "Nazia, you're the only one I trust with this report. Can you stay till nine?" Nazia glowed and stayed.
Bidisha went home and couldn't sleep. That was the third time this month. She had flattered Nazia into staying late for a report she herself had delayed. And last week, when a donor visit went badly, she had let the juniors believe it was a transport problem, not her missed call.
On Monday she called Nazia aside. "I owe you honesty. The report was late because of me. I should have asked plainly, and let you say no. And the donor visit was my mistake."
Nazia looked startled. "I didn't mind staying."
"I know. That's why I have to be careful."

qa.q: What did Bidisha ask Nazia to do on Friday at six?
qa.a: Stay till nine to finish a report.

qa.q: Why couldn't Bidisha sleep that night?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and ashamed, realising she had flattered Nazia into staying late and had hidden her own mistake about the donor visit.

qa.q: What did Bidisha change on Monday?
qa.a: She told Nazia the truth about the delay and the donor visit, and said she should ask plainly and allow a no.

qa.q: How might Nazia see Bidisha after hearing the truth?
qa.a: Nazia may feel startled and a little disappointed, but also respected, and may trust Bidisha more for being honest.

grounding: The protagonist notices she uses juniors' admiration to get late work and protect her image; she stops and is honest about her needs.

subtopic: Being idolised or hated by juniors
passage:
Xin noticed it during the Vancouver team's sprint review. When the demo crashed, she said lightly, "Priscila's module is still new, we'll smooth it out," and everyone nodded. Priscila, who admired her, nodded too, though the crash had come from Xin's own late change.
In the lift afterwards Xin felt sick. She had got used to it: the juniors staying late for her, laughing at her jokes, taking her side. It was pleasant, and she had started to lean on it.
The next morning she messaged the team channel: "Correction on yesterday. The demo crash was my commit, not Priscila's module. Sorry, Priscila." Then she added: "Also, I've been asking people to stay late without saying why. I'm behind on my own tasks. I'll say that directly from now on."
Priscila replied with a thumbs up and, a minute later, "Thanks for saying that 🙏"

qa.q: What caused the demo to crash?
qa.a: Xin's own late change, her commit.

qa.q: What was Xin feeling in the lift after the review?
qa.a: She felt sick with guilt, seeing she had let an admiring junior take the blame to protect her image.

qa.q: How did Xin repair the situation?
qa.a: She corrected the record publicly, apologised to Priscila, and said she would be direct about her own workload instead of leaning on admiration.

qa.q: How might Priscila feel reading the correction?
qa.a: Priscila probably feels relieved and respected, and the thanks suggests her trust in Xin becomes more grounded.

grounding: The protagonist notices she uses juniors' admiration to protect her image and get extra work; she stops and is honest about her needs.
